words: The three points show one real gap: a player who left because the game was a draw for them did not lose, and my deeming reached them. I fix it so only players who actually lost count, and a game that was a draw for any player is left to the draw sentence of 103.1.

replies.words: Fixed: a player for whom the game was a draw is not a loser under the rule, and a game that was a draw for any player is outside the rule and goes by the draw sentence of 103.1.

Fixed: the rule no longer says every early leaver lost. Only a player who left by losing counts as having lost then; one who left because the game was a draw for them is not a loser, and the whole game then goes by the draw sentence.
Fixed in the same way: the rule is stated for games in which no player left with a draw, and says draws, including a draw for one player, are left to the draw sentence of 103.1.

facts.text: A Commander match of several games with three players
In the previous game, two of the three players lost (at different times) and the third player won

case.rule: In a free-for-all multiplayer match of several games, if the previous game was won by one player and no player left it because the game was a draw for them, the losers of that game are the players who left it by losing, each at the moment they lost, and any players still in the game when the winner won, at the moment the game ended. If there is more than one loser, the player who lost first is the loser who chooses who takes the first turn. If several players lost first at the same moment, those players decide among themselves which of them chooses, and if they cannot agree the chooser is picked at random from them. If the previous game was a draw, or was a draw for any player, the draw sentence of 103.1 applies and this rule does not apply. The rule does not apply to team games, or to any game type whose starting player the Comprehensive Rules already settle by their own rule, such as Archenemy games (103.1b) and Supervillain Rumble (904.12c); those stay as they are.
applies_when: a free-for-all multiplayer match of several games (such as a three-player Commander match), not a team game and not a game type whose starting player the CR already settles (such as Archenemy or Supervillain Rumble), where the previous game was won by one player, no player left it because the game was a draw for them, and there was more than one loser

source.excerpt: In a match of several games, the loser of the previous game chooses who takes the first turn.

steps.conclusion: In a match of several games, 103.1 has the loser of the previous game choose who takes the first turn.

source.excerpt: Unlike two-player games, multiplayer games can continue after one or more players have left the game.

steps.conclusion: A multiplayer game can continue after a player has left it, so players can be out of the game at different times before it ends; F2 states that in this game two players lost at different times.

In a free-for-all game with one winner in which no player left because the game was a draw for them, the losers for 103.1 are the players who left by losing and the players still in the game when the winner won. Where there is more than one loser, the player who lost first chooses who takes the first turn; players who lost first at the same moment decide among themselves who chooses, else it is random among them. Draws (whole game or for any player), team games and game types whose starting player the CR already settles (Archenemy, Supervillain Rumble) are outside this stipulation.

source.excerpt: If the previous game was a draw, the player who made the choice in that game makes the choice in this game.

steps.conclusion: If the previous game was a draw, 103.1 has the player who made the choice in that game make the choice in this game; the stipulation does not apply to a draw, so this stays as it is.
